summary: Carney calls Stellantis's sale of its Brampton plant a "betrayal", sets off on a four-summit trip ending in China, and the budget makes museums free for under-25s.
body: Stellantis, the carmaker behind Jeep and Chrysler, announced on Monday that it will sell its idle assembly plant in Brampton to Roshel, a Canadian maker of armoured vehicles.[^1] More than 2,200 workers have been laid off since production stopped in December 2023. On Tuesday Prime Minister Mark Carney called the sale "a betrayal of the workers" and said Canada will "fully enforce our rights", since Ottawa agreed in 2022 to give Stellantis $529 million to retool its Brampton and Windsor plants. Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says the company broke its contract and will meet Unifor and Stellantis in Toronto on Thursday.[^1]

Roshel's chief executive says Brampton residents will get priority for jobs but the company will not rehire all former Stellantis workers. The auto parts industry group says an armoured-vehicle plant would employ "a fraction" of the thousands the car plant once supported. Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre called the sale "yet another Liberal betrayal" and wants Joly fired.[^1]

After Remembrance Day ceremonies today, Carney leaves on an eight-day trip: a European summit in Dublin, the ASEAN summit in Manila, where Canada hopes to finish a trade deal with Southeast Asian countries, the Francophonie summit in Cambodia, and APEC in Shenzhen, China, where he is due to meet Xi Jinping.[^2][^3] The government says it wants new trading partners beyond the US; Conservatives say past trips have brought few real gains.[^2]

For students: in Montreal, Carney highlighted $4 billion for culture in last week's budget, including over $45 million over five years to make national museums free for visitors under 25, and $300 million more for CBC/Radio-Canada.[^4]
differences: The government calls Stellantis's sale a breach of contract and promises legal action; Stellantis says it offered to return support for Brampton's original retooling plan. Conservatives blame the government for the outcome.[^1]
